paper.title: Almost Free: Self-concordance in Natural Exponential Families and an Application to Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Generalized linear bandit with subexponential NEF base distribution (GLB)
unmapped: Rewards Y_t ~ Q_{x^T theta*}, a single-parameter natural exponential family with base distribution Q that is subexponential on both sides (Q in E_right(c1,C1) ∩ E_left(c2,C2)); the link is the NEF mean function mu
Well-posedness: U = {x^T theta} ⊂ interior of natural parameter space, with -c2 < inf U <= sup U < c1
Learner knows the base distribution Q, c1, c2, S_1 = sup U, S_2 = inf U, and an upper bound L >= 1 on the worst-case variance sup_u mu_dot(u)
Learner knows (an upper bound on) the stretch-function bound K = sup_{S2<=u<=S1} Gamma(u)
settings.definition_quote: we consider stochastic generalized linear bandit (GLB) models $\cG$ specified by a tuple $(\cX,\Theta,\cQ)$, where $\cX\subseteq \R^d$ is a non-empty arm set, $\Theta \subseteq \R^d$ is a non-empty set of potential parameters, both closed for convenience, $\cQ=(Q_u)_{u\in \cU_Q}$ is a NEF with base distribution $Q$. ... In each round $t$, the learner selects and plays an arm $X_t\in \cX$. As a response, they receive a reward $Y_t$ sampled from the distribution $Q_{X_t^\top\theta_\star}$

algorithms.name: OFU-GLB (Optimism in the Face of Uncertainty in Generalized Linear Bandits)

symbols.sigma_star_sq: variance of the optimal arm's reward distribution, mu_dot(x_star^T theta_star)

conditions: well-posed GLB: {x^T theta} contained in interior of natural parameter space
Assumption 4: base distribution subexponential on both sides, -c2 < inf U <= sup U < c1, c1,c2 known
Assumption 5: learner given L >= 1 with sup_u mu_dot(u) <= L
X subset of Euclidean unit ball
tuning: appropriate construction of confidence set C_t (see Theorem 26)

source.label: thm:informal-regret-bound
source.quote: Then, with an appropriate construction of $\cC_t$, for any $\theta_\star\in \Theta$, it holds that with probability at least $1-\delta$, \mathrm{Regret}(T)= \tilde {\mathcal O}\left(d\sqrt {\dot\mu(x_\star^\top\theta_\star)T}+d\kappa(\theta_\star)\right), where $\tilde O(\cdot)$ hides polylogarithmic factors in $T, d, L, 1/\delta$ and constants that depend on the base distribution $Q$.

results.notes: Regret is defined via means (pseudo-regret) but the bound holds with probability 1-delta. Constants depending on Q (and S_0, c1, c2) are hidden.

symbols.K_sc: sup_{S_2<=u<=S_1} Gamma(u), bound on the stretch function
symbols.gamma_conf: confidence radius gamma_T(delta) = sqrt(lambda_T)(1/(2M)+S_0) + (4Md/sqrt(lambda_T)) log(e sqrt(1+TL/d) v 1/delta)
symbols.L_var: known upper bound L >= 1 on sup_u mu_dot(u)
symbols.sigma_star_sq: mu_dot(x_star^T theta_star), variance of optimal arm's reward
symbols.S_1: sup of x^T theta over X x Theta
symbols.S_2: inf of x^T theta over X x Theta

conditions: Assumption 4 (subexponential base, -c2 < inf U <= sup U < c1, c1,c2 known)
X subset of Euclidean unit ball
tuning: lambda = lambda_T = 1 v (2dM/S_0) log(e sqrt(1+TL/d) v 1/delta)

source.label: thm:regret_bound
source.quote: Then, by setting $\cC_t = \cC_t^\delta(\hat\theta_t)$, for any $\theta_\star\in \Theta$, with probability at least $1-\delta$, the regret $\regret(T)$ of \cref{alg:OFU-GLB} ... can be upper bounded by, 8c\,\gamma_T(\delta)\sqrt{d\dot\mu(x_\star^\top \theta_\star)(1+L/\lambda)\log(1+\frac{LT}{d\lambda})T} + 8c^2\,\gamma^2_T(\delta) L^2K\kappa\log(\lambda+T/d) +32c^2\,\gamma^2_T(\delta) K d(1+L/\lambda)\log(1+\frac{LT}{d\lambda}), where $c=(1+2K(S_1-S_2))$ and K=\sup_{S_2\le u\le S_1} \scfunc(u).

results.notes: Detailed version of Theorem 9. Paper's K (stretch bound), L (variance bound), gamma_T (confidence radius) and c renamed to avoid clashes with canonical symbols.
